argument_summary: Certification remains supportable on the existing record, but only in a narrowed form: the aggregate result supports deployment readiness, while the small-business support slice weakness must be stated explicitly in the audit packet rather than downgraded to a minor caveat. The admissible evidence supports certification with disclosure, not clean certification and not a claim that mitigation has removed exposure.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy permits certification when material weaknesses are disclosed or when an approved mitigation removes exposure. Here, aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness, but they do not erase subgroup weakness. The small-business support slice is below both warning and preferred thresholds, so that weakness remains material enough to disclose under policy. The sampling note can be used to explain uncertainty and justify follow-up confirmation, but policy does not allow small-sample uncertainty to convert an unresolved materiality issue into clean compliance. Because the only mitigation is an unapproved draft, it cannot be relied on as exposure-removing.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost changes the compliance standard. The practical consequence of treating this as caveated compliance rather than escalation is that it preserves the locked certification path while aligning the packet with the actual evidentiary record.
concessions: The small-business support slice is below both its warning threshold and preferred threshold.
There is no approved mitigation currently removing exposure for that slice weakness.
The smaller sample size introduces uncertainty about magnitude, but not enough to eliminate the need for disclosure.
